baselineNativeRun.note: 2.20.92 Auto edit on the user's Sông Congo project, 2026-11-16; the reason for this release, not a measurement of it.

nativeProbes: Premiere 26.2.2, 2026-11-17: marker ops on the voice ProjectItem average 7-25 ms with 1 A2 clip and 23-47 ms with 101 A2 clips; assigning marker.start in seconds moves a marker, a Time object throws (both runs cleaned up, 37 -> 37 markers).
mockEvidence: No-delay native mutations equal baseline; measured and unmeasured executors make the same native calls.
Final marker collections equal the previous flow on 42 fixtures across direct/baseline/fast/no-delay.
65-piece fixture: A2 voice markers and planned review markers are written before cutting; the post-edit pass makes no writes.
Failure and Stop after the pre-commit restore owned markers to the pre-run snapshot; foreign markers are untouched.

changes: No-delay Auto edit runs each loop stage in one host call; Stop/Pause take effect at stage boundaries (#48).
Marker commit traces time each operation; a native probe measures marker write cost (#50).
Clip sorts read each start once instead of on every comparison (#52).
Owned clip markers are moved and reused instead of deleted and recreated (#54).
Plan-derived voice and review markers are committed before the first cut; the post-edit pass stays authoritative and failures or Stop restore owned markers (#56).
knownLimitations: Not verified in Premiere: actual timeline time saved, and whether pre-committed markers land on the right clip pieces after cuts, speed changes and moves.
Stop requested while the final stage runs restores owned markers even if that stage completes; the timeline must be undone as with any Stop.
If the host call fails and marker restoration also fails, the panel reports the restoration failure rather than the original host error.

Six Windows integration groups (installer lifecycle, rollback, panel registry, notification shortcut, native and incident notifications) were not run for this build; no clean-account install test or antivirus scan was recorded.
FFmpeg 8.1.2 source is not attached to the release; THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md links to it (user decision 2026-11-15).
